payload.title: Wedding Photo App Guide for Collecting Guest Photos
payload.audience: 30s, couples who are interested in destination weddings and luxury experiences, 150k+ AUD budget
payload.reader: An Australian couple in their 30s planning a destination or luxury wedding, many guests travelling, who want every candid photo and video their guests take gathered in one private place, and need to know which type of photo app suits their day, which features matter, how to handle privacy, consent and ownership, and how to make it work at a venue overseas where Wi-Fi and data are uncertain.
payload.goal: Speak with a Wedded Advisor about planning a destination wedding (single primary CTA, placed after the destination weddings section); Wonderland Studio as a soft secondary link for seating charts and RSVPs only.
payload.angle: Page-one results are ranked lists of named apps that date quickly and read like affiliate roundups. We name no apps at all. Instead we explain the five types of guest photo tool (shared album apps, QR code upload pages with no install, disposable camera style apps where photos reveal later, live slideshow displays, and the photographer's own gallery), give a feature checklist a couple can hold any app against, deal plainly with privacy, consent and who owns guest photos with official sources at each claim, and add the part list articles skip: making it work at a destination venue where Wi-Fi and data are questions to ask and guests are spread across time zones.
must_include: Intro, then exactly 4 one-sentence Key takeaways
What a wedding photo app does: gathers guests' photos and videos in one private album the couple controls, alongside (not instead of) the professional photographer

The main types, no app names: shared album apps; QR code upload pages with no install; disposable camera style apps where photos reveal later; live slideshow displays; the photographer's own gallery (what each suits, its trade-offs)

What to look for (checklist): no download needed for guests; full resolution kept; video supported; moderation and who can see the album; downloading everything at the end; how long photos are kept; offline uploads that send later when signal is patchy

Privacy and consent: sharing images of people and children, asking before posting publicly, album visibility settings; official sources (for example OAIC, eSafety Commissioner) linked inline at each claim; general information, not legal advice

Who owns guest photos: copyright usually sits with the person who took the photo; what that means for couples using guest photos; as official sources state it (Attorney-General's Department, legislation.gov.au or similar) linked at the claim; general information only

Setting it up: QR cards on tables and at the entrance; an unplugged ceremony option with the upload invitation saved for the reception; telling guests on the invitation or wedding website (link /expert-advice/wedding-website and /wedding-rsvp-website)

Destination weddings: Wi-Fi and data at the venue framed as questions to ask the venue; offline uploads; guests across time zones uploading after the day and viewing from home; single primary CTA to /wonderland-concierge after this section
FAQ (4 to 6 questions, no figures, no app names)

Close with one Wedded Advisor line using brand-facts.md lines 19 to 30 only (for example one Wedded Advisor start to finish as a single point of contact, working in the couple's time zone), linking /wonderland-concierge; mention Wonderland Studio only as our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs

Internal links: /wonderland-studio, /expert-advice/what-is-wonderland-studio, /expert-advice/best-wedding-planning-apps, /expert-advice/wedding-planning-app-vs-spreadsheet, /expert-advice/wedding-website, /wedding-rsvp-website, /expert-advice/average-cost-wedding-photographer (photographer's gallery and copyright context), /expert-advice/our-favourite-interactive-seating-charts, /wonderland-concierge
avoid: Any app, brand or product name, including in headings, FAQ, alt text and image captions (person's decision)
Any claim that Wonderland Studio shares, collects or displays photos; describe it only as our planning app for seating charts and RSVPs
Links to any 'vs Wonderland Studio' comparison page (/expert-advice/*-vs-wonderland-studio, /expert-advice/weddingwire-vs-the-knot-vs-wonderland-studio)
Prices, free or paid tiers, storage limits, upload caps, statistics or numeric survey results
Research talk in the copy (sources, method, what we could or couldn't find)
Privacy, consent or copyright statements without the official source linked inline at the claim; no legal advice framing
Stating any venue's Wi-Fi or data coverage as fact; frame as questions to ask
Advisor claims beyond brand-facts.md lines 19 to 30
US spelling; em dashes; title or meta title as a question, with colons or dashes
